_comment: Hand-authored. The last 34 bytes no earlier pass claimed: three palette lists and three leads.

regions.name: Palette list: the title screen, 8 palettes
regions.description: A palette list for the walker at bank 7 $D92D (entered at $C05D with the pointer in $18/$19): for list position Y = 0-7 and a value below $FE it far-calls bank 5 $B2E4, which copies palette number A (three colours from the 36 x 3 table at bank 5 $B30A) to $0181 + 3Y; $FE ends the list, $FF skips the position. Positions 0-3 are the four background palettes and 4-7 the four sprite palettes. Read at bank 0 $8321: JSR $8485 (draws the screen), then LDA #$BD / STA $18 / LDA #$82 / STA $19 / JSR $C05D, then JMP $C01B. The list is 08 09 0A 0B 00 01 02 03: background palettes 8-11 (30 26 16, 30 12 01, 30 16 11, 31 21 11) and sprite palettes 0-3. HARDWARE: the title-screen savestate's palette RAM $0181-$0198 holds exactly those eight (8 of 8), and the password-screen savestate's slots 0-3 match too. Found by scanning the ROM for a pointer built from two immediates (LDA #lo / LDA #hi), the search that found the world map: no table anywhere points at it.

regions.name: Palette list: the status screen, 7 palettes and a skip
regions.description: A palette list for the walker at bank 7 $D92D (entered at $C05D with the pointer in $18/$19): for list position Y = 0-7 and a value below $FE it far-calls bank 5 $B2E4, which copies palette number A (three colours from the 36 x 3 table at bank 5 $B30A) to $0181 + 3Y; $FE ends the list, $FF skips the position. Positions 0-3 are the four background palettes and 4-7 the four sprite palettes. Read at bank 5 $84EE, in the status screen's open routine ($84CB): LDA #$C3 / STA $18 / LDA #$84 / STA $19 / JSR $C05D. The list is 05 0F 1F FF 00 01 02 03: background palettes 5, 15 and 31, position 3 skipped (the HUD-colour slot keeps what it had), and sprite palettes 0-3. Read from the code only; there is no status-screen savestate to compare with.

regions.name: Palette-list-shaped table, no reader found
regions.description: 00 01 02 03 05 06 09 0A: eight values, all below 36, which is the shape of a list for the palette walker at $D92D (see bank0.pal_82BD). LEAD: nothing reads it. No absolute or indexed operand names $EEC1-$EECC, no LDA #$C4 / LDA #$EE pair builds the pointer, and no 16-bit word $EEC4 exists anywhere in the ROM. It sits right after an RTS ($EEC3) and before the routine at $EECC (it reads byte 2 of the room record, $E4).

regions.name: Five bytes after the cannon tables, no reader found
regions.description: FE 02 FF 01 00 (signed: -2, 2, -1, 1, 0). They follow tbl_A9B8, the two bytes the handler of types $36/$37 reads with LDA $A982,Y ($A8E0), and precede the five 4 x 4 tile rectangles at $A9BF. The same reader with Y = $38-$3C would land here, but no object of those types is dispatched to that handler, and no other operand in bank 6 names $A980-$A9BE. LEAD: the count of five matches the five rectangles, nothing more.

regions.name: Sound stream fragment, no header points at it
regions.description: 12 E9 82: read as the stream format, a note ($12), a repeat of it with duration index 9 ($E9) and a track end ($82). The song headers at $BEF4 and $BF07 name streams at $BEFF (89 08 38 E7 82, ending at $BF03) and $BF12; no pointer in the song table at $9B74 or in any header names $BF04. LEAD: an unused or cut-off track.

regions.name: Two bytes between two handlers, no reader found
regions.description: 78 64 (120, 100). They follow the JMP $A991 that ends the handler at $B8F8-$B901 and precede the handler at $B904. No operand names $B900-$B904 as a table base. LEAD: padding or an unused pair.
